title: Rex and the Missing Moon Map
style: colourful premium 3D animated family-film illustration, soft rounded forms, rich cinematic lighting, joyful expressive faces
summary: Rex, a cheerful young T-Rex astronaut, and his small robot friend Pip search the Moon for a lost star map. By sharing clues and working together, they find it and follow it home for a well-earned rest.

characters.name: Rex
characters.visualDescription: A small, friendly young T-Rex with mint-green skin, a pale cream belly, three soft darker-green stripes down his back, large warm amber eyes, and a wide happy smile showing tiny rounded teeth. He wears a puffy white spacesuit with orange trim, a round clear helmet, orange boots, and a small orange rocket badge on his chest. His short arms, thick tail, and boots are always fully visible.

characters.name: Pip
characters.visualDescription: A small friendly robot, knee-high to Rex, with a rounded silver body, a single big round blue eye, two thin antennae with tiny yellow lights, short stubby tracks instead of legs, and a small hatch on its chest that glows soft yellow. Pip's whole body and tracks are always fully visible.

cover.narration: Rex and the Missing Moon Map

pages.text: Rex the young T-Rex astronaut loved exploring. Today he landed his little rocket on the silvery Moon, with his best friend Pip the robot rolling happily beside him.
pages.imagePrompt: Wide establishing action shot as a small red-and-white rocket has just landed, with fresh landing marks and a lowering ramp. Rex, a small friendly mint-green young T-Rex with cream belly, three darker-green back stripes and amber eyes, bounds down the ramp in his puffy white spacesuit with orange trim, clear helmet and orange boots. Pip, a knee-high rounded silver robot with one blue eye, yellow-lit antennae and stubby tracks, rolls after him across grey Moon dust. Earth hangs far above the lunar horizon. Whole characters visible.

pages.text: "Time to fly home," said Rex. He reached into his pocket for his star map, which showed the way back to Earth. But the pocket was empty. The map was gone!
pages.imagePrompt: Tight expressive waist-up close shot: Rex freezes beside the rocket ramp and turns his empty spacesuit pocket inside out, eyes wide and mouth surprised. Pip looks up from the lower foreground and scans the empty pocket with a soft blue beam. The rocket doorway glows behind them; the lunar landscape is blurred in the distance.

pages.text: "Don't worry," said Pip kindly. "We can find it together. I saw a sparkly corner near the big crater!" Rex smiled. Clues were much easier with a friend.
pages.imagePrompt: Low over-the-shoulder discovery view from behind Rex: Pip stands on a small ridge in the foreground, projecting a narrow blue pointer towards a huge crater far across the Moon. A tiny paper corner sparkles at the crater rim. Rex turns towards the clue with a relieved smile; long lunar shadows lead the eye into the distance.

pages.text: At the big crater, something glimmered in the dust. It was a shiny corner of paper! As Rex stepped closer, his boot nudged the dust, and the paper slipped downhill.
pages.imagePrompt: Dramatic overhead view looking down into the large crater: Rex and Pip are small figures at the rim, leaning forward as a white map corner slips through disturbed Moon dust and slides down the steep curved wall. Their surprised faces and reaching poses clearly show the sudden movement.

pages.text: Rex tried to reach it, but his arms were too short. Pip rolled after it, but the dusty slope was too steep for little tracks. They stopped and thought together.
pages.imagePrompt: Side-on action scene across the steep crater wall: Rex braces his orange boots at the top and stretches one comically short arm, while below him Pip's tracks skid sideways and leave clear grooves. The map rests visibly just beyond both of them. Show effort, distance and the slope as the obstacle.

pages.text: "I have an idea," said Rex. "You are small and steady. I am tall and strong. If we hold hands, we can reach it together!" Pip beeped happily. Teamwork time!
pages.imagePrompt: Calm planning moment from a medium front angle on level ground: Rex kneels and draws a simple reach plan in the Moon dust with one claw while Pip shines a blue light on the sketch. Rex points from his strong tail and boots to Pip's small gripper; both exchange an excited we-have-an-idea look. The map remains visible far down the slope behind them.

pages.text: Carefully, slowly, Rex held Pip out over the slope. Pip's little gripper arm stretched, stretched, stretched... and caught the paper corner! Up they came together, safe and sound.
pages.imagePrompt: Dynamic diagonal rescue shot from low inside the crater looking upward: Rex lies securely across the rim, boots and tail braced against a rock, holding Pip out over the slope. Pip's extended gripper closes around the fluttering white map at the decisive instant. Moon dust sparkles around them; both faces show concentration and triumph.

pages.text: The map was a little crumpled, but every star was still there. "Look!" said Rex. "The map shows a path to a quiet crater. That sounds like the perfect rest stop."
pages.imagePrompt: Intimate top-down map-reading scene: the recovered crumpled star map fills the centre on a flat Moon rock, lit by Pip's blue eye. Rex's orange-gloved claw and Pip's small gripper point to a dotted route while their happy faces lean in from opposite sides. The crater rim surrounds the composition.

pages.text: They followed the dotted line across the silver hills, past small craters, all the way to their little rocket waiting patiently under the stars.
pages.imagePrompt: Very wide cinematic journey shot across rolling silver hills: Rex strides and Pip rolls along a winding trail of footprints in the lower foreground, following the map towards their small red-and-white rocket glowing on a distant ridge. They pass several different craters under Earthlight; the scale and destination are unmistakable.

pages.text: Rex tucked the map safely away and patted Pip's warm metal head. "We did it together," he said. And the two friends flew home, sleepy, smiling, and ready for the next adventure.
pages.imagePrompt: Warm interior rocket scene, completely different from the Moon exterior: Rex buckles the recovered map into a safe wall pocket, then pats Pip's head as the robot rests in a charging cradle. Through the large curved window the Moon recedes and Earth grows bright ahead. Instrument lights create a cosy bedtime glow.
